entries.name: Basalt Columns

facts.claim: Hexagonal/columnar olivine basalt at Ohira Bay on a south-facing coast of Petre Bay; formed from a ponded lava flow about 80 million years ago (Cretaceous); described as one of the most popular attractions on the islands.
On private property: access needs permission beforehand and payment of an entry fee. Ask your host/accommodation to arrange a trip, or contact Jonathon Reriti, ph 0277050073.
Wikivoyage: 'get a key from Hotel Chathams to open the gate'.

Third-party hiking guide: access via Port Hutt Road, phone ahead and collect a gate key (many accommodation providers hold one), entry fee $25, drive to the end of the road after unlocking the gate, columns a short walk, allow at least an hour.
Moriori once quarried the columns for adzes; the five-sided shape inspired the design of Kopinga Marae.

entries.hours: By arrangement (private land; gate key and permission needed)
entries.cost_status: entry fee confirmed by tourism board (amount not stated); NZD 25 from one undated third-party blog; verify with Jonathon Reriti 0277050073
entries.ticketUrl_note: No operator website exists (private farmland). This is Tourism Chatham Islands' own page for the attraction (loaded, title 'Basalt Columns'); it carries the landowner contact. Orchestrator may prefer null. How to book: ask accommodation host or Hotel Chatham (Wikivoyage says the gate key is held there) or phone the landowner; fee payable on arrival/permission.

entries.name: Point Munning Seal Colony

facts.claim: Point Munning is part of a 47 ha conservation covenant owned by the Muirson family, with public access to watch a seal haul-out/rookery; seals present all year; also birdwatching (Pitt Island shags breed there).
Private land: permission beforehand and an entry fee; contact Muirson family ph 03 3050 022.
Go through the Murchison farm and park at the fence marking the covenant entrance; a short bush walk leads to the beach with a large seal colony; be quiet and don't get close.
Hotel Chatham's Okawa walk (5 h one-way, guided) ends at Mission Bay, with Point Munning a further 2 km.

entries.cost_status: UNVERIFIED: entry fee required but amount not published by any source found; ask Muirson family 03 3050 022. Do not publish a price; 'free' would be wrong.

Port Hutt Rd, 23 km / 50 min drive from Waitangi; book through Hotel Chathams.

entries.name: Awatotara Bush Coastal Walk

facts.claim: Awatotara Walk: 2.5 to 3 hour walk, independent $15 pp or guided $20 pp (minimum 6 people); creek crossings; full-day guided Tuku Tour $80 pp (min 3). Tuku Tours, Tuku Rd, ph +64 3 3050351 (Liz and Bruce Tuanui).

Track through native bush with Chatham pigeon, tui, parakeet, warblers to the rugged coastline; visits Taiko Camp and Gap Sanctuary; private land: permission beforehand and entry fee; tours by arrangement, ph 03 3050351.

Third-party guide: access at the southern end of Waitangi Tuku Road, permission needed (Liz or Bruce 305 0351), access charges apply; Bush to Coast (1-2 h) and Loop (2-3 h) tracks are advanced tramping.

entries.name: German Mission House

facts.claim: Heritage New Zealand Category 1 building; built 1866-1868 by German Moravian missionaries (arrived 1843) of local stone, burnt pipi-shell mortar and akeake lintels and doors; permission from the owner is needed and a charge applies to help cover maintenance.

Open by appointment only; contact Jymy and Tarsha Gregory-Hunt, ph 03 3050 653 or 027 3050 302, Waitangi West Road; alternative: Paddy and Wai 03 3050074. Allow time for a beach walk to basalt boulders.
Wikivoyage: drive through the gate to the cottage; the caretaker (Helen) gives a tour for an entry fee; Waitangi West Road, ph +64 3 3050302.
Third-party guide: ring first (Helen Bint, 305 0501), visiting days Tue-Fri, entry fee $20, about 15 min grass-track walk from the road.

entries.name: Port Hutt

facts.claim: Picturesque bay in a sheltered cove of Whangaroa Harbour on the island's western side, developed as a picnic spot; American scientists observed the 1874 transit of Venus from here; relics including the trawler Thomas Currell rest in the shallows; base of a small crayfishing/pāua industry.
Private land: access needs permission beforehand and an entry fee; ask your host to arrange a day trip; contact ph 03 3050011, chathamseafood@farmside.co.nz.
Wikivoyage: one of the most attractive ports in New Zealand; well-sheltered harbour; historically important.

entries.cost_status: UNVERIFIED: tourism board says an entry fee is payable but gives no amount; no other source found. Do not publish as free.

entries.name: Kaingaroa

facts.claim: Small fishing village with a one-teacher school and a social clubroom; picturesque harbour used by sealers and whalers, boomed with blue cod exports around 1910 and the 1960s crayfish boom; walk to the north-western beach and along hard sandy Kaingaroa Beach; rare Chatham plants in the coastal zone; two memorials to Lieutenant Broughton's 1791 visit.
Wikivoyage: bustling little fishing village on the northern corner; residents prepare a Saturday meal at the Kaingaroa Club (event, not a spot feature).

entries.cost_status: No charge mentioned (public village and beach)

entries.name: Ocean Mail Scenic Reserve

facts.claim: 831 ha of peat dome and wetland at Te Whanga Lagoon, extending over the road to include 4 km of coastal dunes; includes Lakes Wharemanu and Kaimoumi; signs and cattle stops mark each end on the north road to Kaingaroa; a vehicle track about 2 km in leads to a stile and the beach.
Walks: Wetland walk 15-min loop, Aster walk 20-min return, Lake walk 2 h 30 min loop; picnic area on the beach.
Official name Manauea/Ocean Mail Scenic Reserve (DOC); tourism board uses 'Ocean Mail Scenic Reserve'.

entries.cost_status: Public conservation land; no fee mentioned by DOC

entries.name: Nikau Bush Conservation Area

facts.claim: 19 ha of lowland broadleaved forest on the north-western shore of Te Whanga Lagoon with the largest stand of nikau left on the main island; nikau flower spectacularly in December and January; fenced and regenerating since 1981.
Sign on North Road 1.5 km past Pana/Blind Jim's Creek; walk uphill 1 km along the fenceline marked with orange triangles to a stile and sign.
Two loop walks taking about 1 hour; Hotel Chatham gives about 1.5 hours.
Hotel Chatham: Nikau Bush walking time approximately 1.5 hours.

entries.name: Chatham Islands Museum

facts.claim: Opening hours: Monday to Friday 9am to 2pm (most days). Admission $10 per adult; residents free; after-hours group bookings by appointment only. 15 Waitangi Tuku Rd, Waitangi, ph 03 3050 033 ext 3.

Whole-of-islands community museum covering natural and social history; displays of rocks, fossils (including dinosaur), rare birds, Moriori, sealer, whaler, missionary and settler items; large photograph and archive collection; open since 1979 in the Council building.
Conflict: the tourism board page says Mon-Fri 8:30am-4:30pm (except public holidays) with staff onsite till 1pm daily; the museum's own page (preferred) says 9am-2pm.

entries.cost_status: NZD 10 per adult, museum's own site (current)

entries.name: Henga Scenic Reserve

facts.claim: 170 ha reserve with a huge sand-dune system, coastal forest, regenerating vegetation, limestone outcrops and views over Petre Bay; on the west coast; head north from Waitangi on North Road to a pull-off and signage; the route crosses farmland to the reserve.

Walk to a lookout (1 h 30 min return); loop through coastal forest 2 h 30 min; limestone outcrops about 45 min in; shorter 30 min bush walk; tracks easy and signposted; toilet at the start; about 15 minutes' drive from Waitangi; Henga Lodge guests can walk in from the lodge (private land, fee).
Third-party guide: public access is via North Road, the track starts through farmland, with a toilet near the loop start.

entries.cost_status: Public reserve; no fee for DOC access (fee only for Henga Lodge private route)

entries.name: Hapupu National Historic Reserve

facts.claim: DOC: visitors are limited to local whanau; other visitors must book a guided tour with DOC-approved operators. Stay on tracks, do not touch the trees, stand 2 m away.
Wikivoyage: only accessible with concessionaire guides from either Hotel Chathams or Awarakau Farmstays.
Tourism board: public access, but guided trips recommended; short bush walk about 20 minutes, longer walk with the coastal section about 40 minutes.
Hotel Chatham: walk of only about 10 minutes past the kopi rakau momori; Hotel Chatham's guided sightseeing tours are DOC approved.
One of three national historic reserves (DOC, Wikipedia); the tourism board says one of only two.

entries.name: Pitt Island

facts.claim: Visiting Pitt Island is by guided access only, so all trips must be prearranged; access by boat or plane; only accommodation is Flowerpot Bay Lodge; Mt Hakepa has 360-degree views and bronze sculptures, called the first inhabited place to welcome the new day.

Flowerpot Adventures 'Original Pitt Island Day Tour' 2026-27: RRP NZD 495 per person, includes the Cessna flight or boat, 4x4 coach tour and lunch at Flowerpot Bay Lodge; min 8 people (they combine bookings); first plane 9:00 am, back at Chatham about 4:30 pm; 25 min flight; book direct.
Hotel Chatham day tour: up to NZD 500 per person for a group of 4 to 5, includes return airport transfers and lunch at Flower Pot Lodge.
Wikipedia article 'Pitt Island' exists (redirect from Rangiauria), coords -44.2875,-176.22.

entries.name: Kōpinga Marae

facts.claim: Wikivoyage (updated Oct 2018): tours on Wednesdays at 10:00 am; Owenga Road; ph +64 3305 0450.

Tourism board: visitors are welcome to visit and hear the history and Moriori culture but must first book as part of a scheduled group tour; the marae is also the Trust's office so staff cannot receive unscheduled visitors; ph 03 3050 450.

Hokotehi Moriori Trust's own page: opened January 2005, the only Moriori marae, pentagonal design inspired by basalt columns, welcomes visitors with a hokomaurahiri; page lists accommodation and event hire with a BOOK NOW button; no tour price published.
